chunks: Zamzam was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'A spring was caused to flow to it from beneath the Black Stone (al-Hijr), so when the water of the spring prevails, the water of Zamzam becomes sweet.'

key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: Al-Hijr: the Black Stone area or the stone enclosure adjacent to the Ka'bah
key_terms.زَمْزَمَ: The sacred well at the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, believed to have miraculously appeared for Hajar (Hagar) and her son Ismail
key_terms.عَذُبَ: To become sweet, pleasant and palatable (referring to water quality)
key_terms.عَيْنٌ: A natural spring or water source

ai.seo_question: Why does Zamzam water taste sweet according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The Imam explains the miraculous hydrological nature of the Zamzam well, stating that a hidden spring flows into it from beneath the Black Stone (al-Hijr al-Aswad). The sweetness of the Zamzam water is directly tied to when the water of this spring is dominant — an explanation that frames Zamzam's qualities as divinely ordained through natural means.
